plates.title: After Work, We'll Have Each Other
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, ink and faded pigment on aged parchment, drawn as a sequence of small framed scenes connected top to bottom by thin vine-like lines, like marginalia in an old chronicle. At the very top: two hands reaching across an idle workshop of untended machines, captioned THE HUMAN TOUCH. Below, three framed scenes side by side forming a row: left, a wigged courtier gesturing at another man's ceremonial hat before rigid rows of nobles, captioned THE DUKE'S HEADGEAR; center, elegant women seated at a long table with ledgers beneath an opera mask, violin, and hospital cross, captioned THE CHARITY BOARD; right, working men crowded around a corner store counter with scattered dice and cards under a dim lamp, captioned GAMBLING AT THE CORNER STORE. Beneath that same row, three more small scenes directly under each: under the courtier, his shadow on the wall shown as a hunched ape baring its teeth, captioned ARISTOCRATS ARE CHIMPANZEES; under the charity women, one flushed woman mid-confession with a hand half-raised to her mouth, captioned THAT ILLUSION OF BEING USEFUL; under the laborers, rowhouses being torn down by wrecking machinery as families watch, captioned THE DESTRUCTION OF THE WEST END. All three columns funnel downward into a single scene: three circles of whispering figures — a prince, a matron, a laborer — joined by one braided cord, captioned THREE CIRCLES OF GOSSIP. From this convergence, the cord splits into a new row flowing downward: a craftsman holding up a finished object to admiring strangers, captioned RESPECT FOR WHAT WE DO, beside a tally board of working figures with nine of ten marked by a small star, captioned 85 IN 100 SATISFIED. These two converge at the bottom into a final modest scene: a figure at a writing desk looking back up the page toward the idle machines at the very top, captioned I LIKE MY JOB. Use muted browns, ochres, and faded blue-greens, fine ink linework, hand-lettered capitals beneath each scene only, generous bare parchment between scenes, no other lettering anywhere on the page.

plates.title: Versailles, Salons, and Apes
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, ink and muted pigment on aged parchment, continuing the register of the overview page. Open at the top with the overview's own vignette for this part: a vast glittering candlelit hall of courtiers in silk, with four faint ghostly pillars fading behind it, captioned THE GREATEST AGE OF LIGHT. Beneath it, a courtier pointing accusingly at another man's hat before seated dukes, captioned THE DUKE'S HEADGEAR. The scene flows down into a richly furnished salon where guests whisper behind fans while a thinker holds an unread book, captioned THE SALON'S IDLE PHILOSOPHER. From this, two branches: to one side, a reader at a desk beside a tall stack of leather memoirs comparing open pages, captioned A STACK OF MEMOIRS; directly below the salon, a Russian court scene of figures murmuring behind raised hands and pointing across the room, captioned WHO SPOKE TO WHOM. This leads down to a nobleman standing proudly before his family's coat of arms, straightening his collar, captioned DIGNITY IN THE FAMILY CREST, which flows into a cluster of courtiers eyeing each other sidelong in a corridor, their postures echoing apes watching for challenge, captioned TRACKING RANK AND CHALLENGE. At the very bottom of the page, the grand hall returns, now half in shadow, with an open door and a plain undecorated field visible beyond it, captioned NOT THE ONLY PATH. Render in fine ink linework with muted browns, golds, and dull blue-greens, generous bare parchment between scenes, hand-lettered capital titles beneath each vignette only, vines or thin connecting lines linking the scenes top to bottom in reading order, no other lettering anywhere on the page.

plates.title: Why Work Gives Respect
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, ink and muted pigment on aged parchment, continuing the same hand and palette as the earlier plates. Open at the top with the overview's own vignette for this part: a crossroads signpost where one path runs from a family crest toward a workshop door, captioned AN ALTERNATIVE ROAD. Below it, branching into a row of four small scenes: ordinary workers sweeping, stacking, and filing with small contented faces, captioned CONTENT IN DULL WORK; a factory worker at a conveyor line reaching toward a ladder up to a raised walkway, captioned WANTING THE PROMOTION; a young man behind a wine counter holding a glass to the light with a faint world map behind him, captioned THE SOMMELIER'S WINDOW; and an elderly couple telling their life story to a young writer with a notebook, surrounded by small tools and ribbons, captioned A LIFE'S WORK RECALLED. All four scenes funnel downward into a single image: a gate guarded by two robed figures scrutinizing a newcomer before a walled enclosure, captioned GUARDING THE GATE. From this, the page flows down into three scholars in plain coats seated in quiet discussion, with a handshake between ordinary townsfolk visible through a window behind them, captioned THE SCOTTISH PHILOSOPHERS. At the very bottom, a modest figure at a writing desk, pen in hand, with a small window beside them showing both the workshop and the distant gate, captioned I LIKE MY JOB. Render in fine ink linework, muted browns, ochres, and dull blue-greens, generous bare parchment between scenes, thin connecting vine-lines in reading order top to bottom, hand-lettered capital titles beneath each vignette only, no other lettering anywhere on the page.
